title: Do Safety Policies Make Falsifiable Predictions? A Commitment-Tracking Harness

original_idea.body: Do Safety Policies Make Falsifiable Predictions? A Commitment-Tracking Harness

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible accountability chain but the link from a falsifiability-rate dataset to reduced catastrophic risk skips steps.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Clear inherited methodology (parse text, LLM-classify, cross-reference cards); novice with mentor can execute on public docs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable (structured dataset + falsifiability rate) with few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public-text accountability work labs will not do about themselves; no internal access.

novelty.reasoning: Commitment trackers exist but the falsifiability-classification angle may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Commitment-tracking exists but the testable/falsifiable framing may be underexplored.
